newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude seen continuing to strengthen.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-NYMEX crude seen continuing to strengthen.

text.p: NEARBY MONTH CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI-14 * MA-10 * MA-20
----------------- VIEWS FROM THE MARKET - June 30 -------------
* If WTI can tick above resistance at $19.75 the market should see a test of the short term down-trend line at $19.89.
* A bullish convergence of the 10 and 20-day moving averages flags room for further gains.
* A concerted move up again today could trigger short-covering with many dealers still playing the market from the short side.

NYMEX crude futures are seen continuing to strengthen with some technical indicators putting up bullish flags while short-covering against the expiry of July products contracts could add further upside impetus, analysts said.
GNI Research said in their daily report that if WTI can tick above resistance at $19.75 the market should see a test of the short term down-trend line at $19.89.
"After this it should be plain sailing until $20.53, and possibly even a threat of the long term downtrend at $20.89," they said.
A bullish convergence of the 10 and 20-day moving averages flagged room for further gains but the 14-day RSI at 50 percent remains firmly stuck in neutral territory.
Analysts said any concerted move to the upside again today could trigger short-covering with many players still playing the market from the short side.

"Friday's strength saw us initially doing some scaled up selling, but we remain short and a move above $19.64 or a buying extreme today could force us to cover our shorts," Fennella Graham at MeesPierson said.
Al Graham at Elliott Wave International, Gainesville, Georgia said, "The choppy rise from $18.65 is an ugly correction of the decline from $21.35-$18.65 and refuses to die easily.
"There is still an off-chance that this correction was completed at $19.75, but that's a gamble," he adds.

On heating oil Al Graham said: "The price action over the past couple of days has broken above the downtrend line defining the large decline from 57.15 and the choppy rise from 51.10 is correcting that decline and seems intent on climbing a little higher".
He saw the short term trend remaining up until trendline support near 52.75 cents a gallon is taken out.
"The market remains strong even though the preparation is mostly negative," Fenella Graham said.
A similar corrective uptrend is in place on unleaded gasoline but Al Graham said that though the short term trend will remain up gains could totally retrace once the trend is completed.
--Colin Wooster, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7456
